To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the organization of a national health system is a function of the degree of inequality in the country ; 2) health care systems are more likely to be organized around a public insurance system in more egalitarian countries, and more likely to be privatized in more unequal societies ; 3) this relationship is stronger in countries where health care is a public good, and weaker in countries where health is a private good.

(i) there are two main dimensions along which health care systems can be organized, namely the degree of regulation of the health care market and the degree to which the system relies on private or public financing; (ii) the degree of regulation and the degree of public financing of health care are both negatively associated with income inequality; and (iii) the degree of public funding of health care is positively associated with the level of income, whereas there is no clear association between income and the degree of regulation
In summary, our research is concerned with
the organization of health care systems and how it varies across countries, and the factors that explain this variation.
how health care is organized and financed in different countries.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the differences between health care systems across countries are mainly due to the differences in the political, economic, social and cultural environment of the countries and not due to the differences between the health care systems.
the health care system is organized differently in different countries because of the different values and priorities of the citizens of each country.

the health system organization in a given country is a function of the income level, the income inequality, the aversion to inequality, the degree of social capital, the level of trust in government and the level of corruption.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed and tested the first model of health system choices, and we have done so using a new and promising methodology for the study of public policies.
we have tried to show that the organization of the health care system is not an exogenous parameter, but that it is the result of a set of choices made by the government.
health care systems are the result of the interaction between the political economy of the country and the characteristics of the health care market.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the organization of the health care system is a function of the country's income level and the degree of aversion for inequality, with the latter being more important than the former.
health system organization varies across countries according to their level of income inequality.

the organization of a national health system is the result of two different policies : the redistribution of income between healthy and sick people and the regulation of the production and delivery process of health care.
